output.brief: The jump in chilled write-offs is most likely caused by the night receiving cut, not by Haverlow. Since the late-July cut from six to four night operatives, chilled pallets now wait about 3 hours 52 minutes to reach a chamber, up from 44 minutes. They wait in unrefrigerated dock lanes that average 15–17°C. Night write-off rates rose from 0.6% to 2.9% for every supplier, while day rates stayed flat. Haverlow's trailer data shows product at 2.4–3.5°C when the doors opened, and the trailers were emptied about 3 hours before the 6.5–8°C probe readings were keyed in. Those readings therefore reflect warming on the dock, not the load as delivered. The chambers held temperature. Don't raise the chargeback or move volume. Restore the night team to six, cap dock-to-chamber time, and track it weekly from scan data. Keep the receiving probe, since it is how this was found. The rise in Corriebank credits coincides with their move to self-certified claims, but the evidence doesn't show whether any claims were over-claimed. Pull a sample of their claims and trace them to lots and receiving shift before changing credit terms. I'm fairly confident (about 85%) in the main finding.
